title: The guaranteed share and the balance after it have no field, no field identifier and no governed row, so the element of a closed guarantee has no published basis
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-019 Data table; TC-E4-019-02, TC-E4-019-03); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3.md (A2.7.1 to A2.7.4.4, R-GUA-19, R-GUA-26, R-GUA-27, BR-S3-007); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2.md (T3.1, T3.2, T4, T-A.2); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md (R-GUA-19, R-GUA-22, R-GUA-23, R-GUA-24, R-GUA-25, R-GUA-26, R-GUA-27); _work/msr/context/S3.md (ownership rows)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 5 and 6; s7 Target reading; s8 BR2, BR3; s11 Data; s12.5; s13 Database; CON s3 Preconditions; s7 AC1, AC3; s11 Data; s12.1, s12.5, s13
description: Both close criteria turn on one number, the balance after the guaranteed share, and neither the share nor the balance has a home in the target. The legacy Data table names recovery_case, timer, v_ace_account, v_ace_payment, guarantee_claim and decision_log_entry with their field ranges, and guarantee_claim stops at status (DF-TRT-022) and paid_amount (DF-TRT-021) with no share, no balance and no position. TSD S3 T3.1 gives guarantee_claim DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022 only, and TSD S3 T3.2 gives the claim two lists of values and neither carries a share. The routing logic states the conditions as "the balance after the guaranteed share is zero" for R-GUA-26 and "greater than zero" for R-GUA-25 and names no governed row, no field and no calculation for either value; the FSD repeats the conditions in words and adds BR-S3-007, which only forbids writing a business value in code. The two stories therefore compose the balance per calculation from the balance read at the ACE batch date and the share the answered row names, carry both only in the element of the contract, and add no column.
evidence: TSD S3 T3.1: guarantee_claim DF-TRT-015 id to DF-TRT-022 status, with no share and no balance; TSD S3 T3.2: LOV-CLAIM-STATUS and LOV-CLAIM-TYPE only; FSD S3 A2.7.3.1: R-GUA-26 condition "the balance after the guaranteed share is zero" with no row identifier; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-GUA-25 and R-GUA-26: the same condition in words, no governed row; legacy RWB-E4-019 Data table: guarantee_claim "id, case_id, claim_type, claim_deadline, claimed_amount, filed_at and 2 more"; context pack S3: one table, guarantee_claim
owner_role: Data owner of the Logical Data Model with the business analyst of module S3 and the owner of the rwb-decision rule registry
proposed: Publish the share basis as a governed reference row of the GUARANTEE rule set and, if the balance after the share must be auditable as a value, allocate a field identifier for it in the Logical Data Model; until then the composition of ASM-B2-S3-007-1 stands and the element carries it

title: The rules close the guarantee and close the case, while LOV-CLAIM-STATUS has no closed value and the case closure is outside the service
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md (R-GUA-19, R-GUA-25, R-GUA-26, R-GUA-27); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2.md (T3.2 LOV-CLAIM-STATUS, T4, T6.1); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3.md (A2.7.3.1, Requirements served REQ-S3-003); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-019 AC2, AC3, Screen and states); _work/msr/context/S3.md (ownership rows)
section: APP s4 Flow steps 6 and 7; s7 Target reading; s8 BR7, BR8; s9; s11 Data; s12.7; s15; CON s2 Business rationale; s7 AC3, AC4; s11 Data; s12.1, s12.7, s15
description: R-GUA-26 says "close the guarantee and close the case" and moves the case to GUARANTEE_CLOSED, and R-GUA-19 and R-GUA-27 say "close the guarantee" while moving the case to RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE. Nothing in the target carries a closed guarantee: LOV-CLAIM-STATUS offers PREPARING, FILED, DEFECT, PAID and REJECTED, guarantee_claim has no closure column, and the ownership rows give S3 one table, guarantee_claim, with the case, its status and its closure belonging to rwb-case. A reader therefore cannot tell whether a closed guarantee is a claim status, a case status or a separate record, and the legacy screen offers one state list, "Not due; due; submitted; paid; refused", with no closed state either. The stories record the close as the claim result plus the GuaranteeClose element with its closing basis, and leave the case closure to rwb-case, which applies GUARANTEE_CLOSED or RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE from the stage report; no value is added to LOV-CLAIM-STATUS and no case row is written.
evidence: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-GUA-26: from SUBROGATION_POSITION, event BALANCE_SATISFIED, action "Close the guarantee and close the case", to GUARANTEE_CLOSED; TSD S3 T3.2: LOV-CLAIM-STATUS PREPARING, FILED, DEFECT, PAID, REJECTED; TSD S3 T3.1: no closure field; legacy RWB-E4-019 Screen and states: SCR-17 "Not due; due; submitted; paid; refused"; context pack S3 ownership rows: table guarantee_claim, no case table
area: Business rules; data model; service boundary
owner_role: Solution architect of S3 with the owner of P3 rwb-case and the business analyst of module S3
proposed: Keep the claim inside its published list and the closing basis in the element, as the stories do; if a claim-level closed value is wanted, add it to LOV-CLAIM-STATUS through the reference-data owner, and confirm with P3 that GUARANTEE_CLOSED is the case status the parent applies

title: The subrogation position the feature must record has no entity, no field and no identifier in the target
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3.md (A2.7.1 intent, A2.7.2, Requirements served REQ-S3-003); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2.md (T3.1, T3.3); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md (R-GUA-23, R-GUA-24); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-019 AC1, Data table); _work/msr/context/S3.md (ownership rows)
section: APP s1 Story; s7 Target reading; s11 Data; s13 Database; CON s7 AC1, AC3; s11 Data; s13 Database
description: REQ-S3-003 says a guarantee payment that clears the balance "closes the case and records the subrogation position", R-GUA-23 and R-GUA-24 say "record the TCG share against the case for all future recoveries", and the legacy criterion AC1 says the close "records the position". No source gives the position a home: TSD S3 T3.1 has guarantee_claim only, with no share and no position; TSD S3 T3.3 gives the claim one relationship, to recovery_case by case_id; the ownership rows give S3 one table, and recovery_case belongs to rwb-case with DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023 as the legacy data table names them. The stories record the position as the GuaranteeClose element of this contract against the claim, with the share where the answered row names it, and state that a position record of its own would have to be defined first; the subrogation state itself is entered by the sibling story RWB-S3-E4016-APP.
evidence: FSD S3 requirements served: REQ-S3-003 "closes the case and records the subrogation position"; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-GUA-23 and R-GUA-24: "Record the TCG share against the case for all future recoveries", to SUBROGATION_POSITION, no field; TSD S3 T3.1 and T3.3: guarantee_claim and one relationship, no position entity; legacy RWB-E4-019 AC1 and Data table: "records the position", six entities, none a position
owner_role: Data owner of the Logical Data Model with the business lead of module S3
proposed: Publish the subrogation position as a field group with its own identifiers, or confirm that the closing element of this contract is the position record and that all future recoveries read it there; the sibling story RWB-S3-E4016-APP enters the state

title: The trigger of the close step is unnamed: the FSD offers a batch, an event or a timer, and no source says which reaches this feature
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3.md (A2.7.2 step 1, A2.7.4.4, A2.7.3.1); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2.md (T4, T5.3); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md (R-GUA-19, R-GUA-26, R-GUA-27); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-019 AC1, Endpoints); _work/msr/context/S3.md (Temporal slides, connection matrix row S3)
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s4 Flow step 1; s7 Target reading; s12.2, s12.4, s12.9; s19; CON s7 AC4; s12.2, s12.4
description: FSD S3 A2.7.2 gives the step one trigger line, "receives its trigger: a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer", and its background-event table says "No background event"; the routing logic enters the three rows on the events RESUBMISSION_NOT_POSSIBLE, BALANCE_SATISFIED and LOSS_RECORDED and names no system, no timer and no message that produces them; TSD S3 T5.3 gives the module no event and the ownership rows give S3 no job and no event. The two stories therefore enter the close on the case signal the parent CaseWorkflow forwards, carrying the case status, the claim id and the payment reference, and name no message, no timer type and no subscription of their own. The connection matrix row of S3 in the context pack shows it listening to P6 and P8 and calling P7 by Temporal activity, which is consistent with the case signal sourcing the payment outcome from the payment service.
evidence: FSD S3 A2.7.2: step 1 "Receives its trigger: a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer"; FSD S3 A2.7.4.4: "None; no background event"; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-GUA-19, R-GUA-26, R-GUA-27: events named, producer not named; TSD S3 T5.3: "None"; context pack S3 ownership rows: events 0, jobs 0; context pack slide 13: S3 row, P6 "T E", P8 "E", P7 "T"
owner_role: Solution architect of S3 with the owner of P8 rwb-payment and the owner of P3 rwb-case
proposed: Confirm that the close is entered on the case signal the parent forwards once the payment service has matched and posted the guarantee payment, and publish the event or timer that starts it; if a subscription is wanted it becomes a named event with its schema and its DP-09 dependency

title: Architecture v5 gives the recovery.v_ace_* views to rwb-source-data alone, while these stories read three of them through the service's own login under DP-05
source: _work/msr/context/S3.md (naming rules, slides 8 and 13, DP-05); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.5 DP-05, R3 source precedence); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3.md (A1.1 constraints, A2.7.3.1 VR-S3-007-1); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-019 Data table)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s8 BR4; s11 Data; s12.7; s13 Pattern application; s17; CON s3 Preconditions; s7 AC2; s12.5; s17
description: Architecture v5 slide 8 states that the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views are read only by rwb-source-data, and the same slide describes one schema and one login per service. DP-05 of the Template and Rules allows two readings, rwb-source-data's contract or "the service's own ACE views", and the Work Package records no contract dependency on P1 for this legacy key, so the second reading is the only one that keeps the story on its lane. The legacy Data table names v_ace_account with DF-ACE-001 to DF-ACE-042 and v_ace_payment with DF-ACE-043 to DF-ACE-054, and FSD VR-S3-007-1 names v_ace_batch_status, so the step needs three of the views. The stories read them SELECT only at the ACE batch date through this service's login, keep no copy, and record the grant as the working read of ASM-B2-S3-007-5; the conflict with slide 8 is not resolved by the stories and is left open for the architecture owner.
evidence: Context pack S3 slide 8: "ACE schemas and the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views (read only by rwb-source-data)"; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-05: "Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views", dependency added none; legacy RWB-E4-019 Data table: v_ace_account and v_ace_payment; FSD S3 A2.7.3.1 VR-S3-007-1: v_ace_batch_status; split plan: no C dependency on P1 for RWB-S3-E4019-APP
owner_role: Solution architect with ACE and its DBA and the owner of P1 rwb-source-data
proposed: Confirm the SELECT-only grant of the three views to this service's login, or move the reads behind a contract of rwb-source-data and add the C dependency; the stories change only the reader, not the composition or the element
